site.welcome: explore what I'm thinking and learning about in this little corner of the internet.
site.about:
A digital garden is a website where thoughts are allowed to be unfinished. Instead of polished posts in reverse order, it's a growing pile of notes, photos and links that get connected to each other over time — more like a notebook you tend than a blog you publish.

I started this one because most of what I think about never makes it anywhere. It gets said once, or sketched on something I lose. Here it gets planted: I write a thought down, and the garden names it, files it, and finds the other thoughts near it. I don't organize anything. When it gets something wrong, I nudge it.

Every thought starts as a seedling. Some grow roots into other topics. A few become evergreen. Most stay small, and that's fine — the point is that they're here, next to each other, where I can wander back through them.

thoughts.text:
Light serifs feel warmer than bold ones.

Saw it on a café menu. Bold felt like shouting, light felt like talking. Probably more about the contrast with the body text than the serif itself.

Connects to [[Contrast sets the mood]]: a light serif next to a steady sans is a conversation. Two heavy faces is an argument.
thoughts.title: Light serifs feel warmer than bold ones

thoughts.text:
Grids I keep coming back to.

Six columns, big gutters, one thing that breaks the grid on purpose. Every time I try something cleverer I come back to this.
